title: Ratio, Rate and Financial Mathematics
summary: Solve problems with direct and inverse proportion, and with commission, rentals, loans, hire purchase, exchange rates, inflation, and simple and compound interest.

notes.text: Two quantities $x$ and $y$ are in **direct proportion** if $\frac{y}{x}$ is constant: when $x$ doubles, $y$ doubles. They are in **inverse proportion** if $x \times y$ is constant: when $x$ doubles, $y$ halves.

notes.caption: Comparing direct and inverse proportion
rows: A curve (hyperbola) that gets closer to both axes
Cost of petrol and number of litres
Speed and time for a fixed distance

notes.title: Worked example 1: inverse proportion
notes.problem:
(a) A trip takes 3 hours at 80 km/h. How long does it take at 120 km/h?
(b) $x$ and $y$ are inversely proportional, and $y = 15$ when $x = 4$. Find $y$ when $x = 6$.

notes.text: **Commission** is money paid to a salesperson as a percentage of the value of what they sell. An estate agent who earns 6% commission on a R850 000 house earns $0{,}06 \times 850\ 000 = \text{R}51\ 000$.
A **rental** is a fee paid to use something you do not own, such as a flat, a car or a sound system. Rentals often have a fixed part and a part that depends on use.

notes.title: Worked example 2: car hire
notes.problem: A car-hire company charges R350 per day plus R3 per kilometre. Thandeka hires a car for 3 days and drives 420 km. What does she pay?

notes.text: A **budget** is a plan that lists expected income and expenses. Fixed expenses (rent, school fees) stay the same each month; variable expenses (electricity, food) change. A budget helps you avoid spending more than you earn.
Simple interest, loans and hire purchase

notes.caption: Simple interest: A = final amount, P = principal, i = annual rate as a decimal, n = number of years

notes.title: Worked example 3: hire purchase
notes.problem: A laptop costs R9 000 cash. On hire purchase, a 10% deposit is paid and the balance is charged 15% simple interest per year over 2 years, paid in equal monthly instalments. Calculate the monthly instalment.

notes.text: With **compound interest**, the interest earned each year is added to the investment, and the next year's interest is calculated on this bigger amount. You earn **interest on interest**, so the money grows faster than with simple interest.

notes.title: Worked example 4: year by year and by formula
notes.problem: R5 000 is invested at 8% per year, compounded annually. Calculate the amount after 3 years.

notes.title: Worked example 5: simple versus compound
notes.problem: Compare R10 000 invested for 3 years at 10% per year (a) simple interest and (b) compound interest.

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: In $A = P(1 + i)^n$, only the bracket is raised to the power $n$. Calculate $(1{,}08)^3$ first, then multiply by $P$. Typing $5\ 000 \times 1{,}08^3$ on a calculator does this correctly; $(5\ 000 \times 1{,}08)^3$ does not.

**Inflation** is the general increase in prices over time. It works like compound interest: if inflation is 6% per year, a loaf of bread costing R18 will cost about $18 \times 1{,}06^2 = \text{R}20{,}22$ in two years.

notes.title: Worked example 6: exchange rates
notes.problem: The exchange rate is £1 = R23,40. (a) What does a £250 flight cost in rand? (b) How many pounds do you get for R10 000?

items: Direct proportion: $\frac{y}{x}$ constant, straight line through the origin. Inverse proportion: $xy$ constant.
Commission is a percentage of sales; rentals often have a fixed and a usage part.
Simple interest: $A = P(1 + in)$, interest on the principal only.
Compound interest: $A = P(1 + i)^n$, interest on interest, so it grows faster.
Hire purchase: deposit, then interest on the balance, repaid in equal instalments.
Inflation increases prices like compound interest; convert currencies by multiplying or dividing by the exchange rate.

questions.explanation: Compound interest earns interest on previous interest, so after the first year it always gives more.

questions.prompt: The graph of two quantities in direct proportion is a straight line through the origin.
questions.explanation: $y = kx$ is a straight line through $(0;\ 0)$.

questions.prompt: The exchange rate is £1 = R23,40. How many rand is £250?
Car hire costs R350 per day plus R3 per kilometre. Calculate the cost of hiring a car for 3 days and driving 420 km.
A loan of R8 000 is taken at 12% per year simple interest for 2 years and repaid in 24 equal monthly instalments. Calculate the monthly instalment, to the nearest cent.

R10 000 is invested for 3 years at 10% per year.
(a) Calculate the final amount with simple interest.  (1)
(b) Calculate the final amount with interest compounded annually.  (2)
(c) How much more does the compound interest investment earn?  (1)
R2 000 is invested at 5% per year, compounded annually. Without using the formula, calculate the amount at the end of each of the first two years, and the interest earned in the second year.
questions.memo:
Year 1: $2\ 000 \times 1{,}05 = \text{R}2\ 100$ ✓ (1)
Year 2: $2\ 100 \times 1{,}05 = \text{R}2\ 205$ ✓ (1)
Interest in year 2: $\text{R}105$ (more than the R100 in year 1) ✓ (1)

questions.prompt: A laptop costs R9 000 cash. On hire purchase, you pay a 10% deposit, and the balance is charged 15% simple interest per year over 2 years. The balance plus interest is paid in 24 equal monthly instalments. Calculate the monthly instalment.
questions.memo:
Deposit R900; balance R8 100 ✓ (1)
Interest $= 8\ 100 \times 0{,}15 \times 2 = \text{R}2\ 430$ ✓ (1)
Total $= \text{R}10\ 530$ ✓ (1)
Instalment $= 10\ 530 \div 24 = \text{R}438{,}75$ ✓ (1)

questions.prompt: A journey takes 3 hours at an average speed of 80 km/h. How long will the same journey take at 120 km/h? Is this direct or inverse proportion?
questions.memo:
Inverse proportion (faster speed, less time) ✓ (1)
$240 \div 120 = 2$ hours ✓ (1)
